title: Hybrid Onramp & Interop Workshop — Lyrica Tech
summary: High-level discovery focused on hybrid hosting options (hosted/dedicated/private), integration surface (SDKs, gateway/proxy patterns), and observability hooks. Customer is evaluating a pilot with LangChain-based agents and wants clear rate-limit/quotas behavior and on-prem compatibility. Action items and next steps agreed: send pricing + deployment checklist, run small bench with their LangChain stack, and share SOC2 and SSO docs.
topics: Gateway / proxy patterns and on-prem onramp
header:
Date: 2026-04-20
Time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~58 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE), Marcus Lee (Redwood SE), Aisha Townsend (Redwood CSM); Jared Kim (CTO, Lyrica), Priya Desai (Platform), Carlos Mendez (Security), Evelyn Park (ML)
transcript:
[00:00] Samira: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I think we have about an hour. I'm Samira, AE at Redwood Inference, Marcus is our SE, Aisha's on for ops. Can each of you do a quick intro?
[00:08] Jared: Jared Kim, CTO at Lyrica. We're building an internal agent layer for customer support and internal docs, mostly LangChain right now.
[00:14] Priya: Priya, platform, I own infra and deployment decisions.
[00:18] Carlos: Carlos, security. We'll be owning compliance and keys.
[00:21] Evelyn: Evelyn, ML eng, building few pipelines.
[00:24] Marcus: Great, thanks. Quick agenda: map your integration surface, talk hosting options (hosted, dedicated, private), gateway and proxy patterns, rate limits/quotas, and observability.
[00:33] Jared: Our biggest constraint is data residency and audit logs. We have PII queries and legal wants logs for 1 year. We also need SSO to be enforced for access.
[00:43] Aisha: Are you considering on-prem or VPC?
[00:46] Priya: Ideally we want a VPC deployment first, maybe private control plane with our own KMS. On-prem is possible if the pilot goes well.
[00:55] Marcus: That lines up with Redwood Private offering — private control plane and on-prem option. For KMS we integrate with customer KMS/HSM, but we'll want to validate key policies.
[01:03] Carlos: We need SOC 2 evidence, encryption at rest, and auditability; also RBAC for different teams.
[01:09] Samira: We'll share SOC 2 pack and our security whitepaper after this call.
[01:13] Evelyn: Quick question — we rely on LangChain and LlamaIndex. How do your SDKs fit?
[01:18] Marcus: Our Python SDK is compatible with LangChain's LLM interface; we also provide a dedicated connector for LlamaIndex in our examples repo. Some of the code paths are async, and we have streaming support.
[01:27] Evelyn: Are there examples for KV cache handling? We use long context with local KV cache in LangChain.
[01:32] Marcus: We have KV cache guidance but note: some of the auto-transcribed docs show "KV cash" which is confusing — sorry. The runtime exposes prefix caching and a KV cache hook. In hosted mode we handle prefix caching automatically, in private you'd manage the cache in your environment or use our managed cache option in Dedicated.
[01:50] Priya: For the gateway/proxy layer — we have an internal gateway that handles auth and routing. We want to put Redwood behind it; any gotchas?
[01:56] Marcus: Common patterns: 1) Front Redwood with your gateway and use API key passthrough; 2) use our sidecar proxy in VPC to keep traffic internal; 3) hybrid where some calls go hosted and fallback to Dedicated. You mentioned quotas — do you want rate limits on a per-tenant basis?
[02:12] Priya: Yes, per-tenant and per-route. We'd like burst capacity for high concurrency windows.
[02:18] Marcus: We support token- and request-based quotas. For Dedicated we can enforce per-customer quotas via routing policies. In Hosted you'd rely on API key scoping and rate-limit headers, and we can wire webhooks for quota exhaustion.
[02:32] Jared: How deterministic are the rate-limit headers? We need programmatic enforcement in our gateway.
[02:36] Marcus: Headers are emitted consistently; sometimes latency in propagation for policy changes may be a few seconds. For strict enforcement we recommend an edge-side cache in your gateway that respects X-Redwood-Quota headers and a fallback to a cache TTL.
[02:50] Carlos: On audit logs, can you provide token-level traces or only top-level request logs?
[02:55] Marcus: We provide both. Token-level traces are available in Dedicated/Private with your retention config; Hosted gives per-request metadata and optional redaction. We also integrate with observability hooks — you can push spans to your tracing system.
[03:08] Evelyn: Do you have an OpenTelemetry integration?
[03:10] Marcus: Yes, we emit OTLP spans and have examples for Datadog/Tempo. There's also SDK-level tracing you can toggle.
[03:18] Priya: For LangChain, our pipeline orchestrates calls in parallel to multiple LLMs. How does Redwood handle bursty parallel calls?
[03:26] Marcus: Our serving runtime has continuous batching and autoscaling. For Dedicated we can reserve capacity and guarantee throughput; for Hosted there are soft limits and fair-queueing. We can show a benchmark.
[03:38] Jared: Bench first? We want to see latency P95 for 2k concurrent short (256-token) calls.
[03:44] Marcus: We can run a focused bench. We'll need a sample prompt set and target concurrency; we recommend starting with a 500 concurrent run to tune batching parameters.
[03:55] Samira: Action: we'll set up a pilot bench using your LangChain agent patterns. I'll follow up to collect the prompt set.
[04:03] Priya: On deployment automation — does your Dedicated offering support our Terraform stack?
[04:08] Marcus: Yes, we have Terraform modules and Helm charts for on-prem. For VPC Private, we provide CloudFormation & Terraform templates.
[04:16] Carlos: About KMS — how are keys stored in hosted mode? We want to use our KMS and not have keys leave our control.
[04:22] Marcus: For Private and Dedicated we support external KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, HashiCorp Vault). In Hosted we offer customer-managed keys via BYOK flows for some regions; we'll confirm region availability.
[04:34] Evelyn: Any gotchas with streaming and function calling combined with LangChain? We've had session reorder issues.
[04:41] Marcus: Streaming + function calling can add complexity to reassembly; our SDK provides helpers to rehydrate streams and some LangChain examples show recommended patterns. There are still edge cases for partial function results and we recommend idempotency keys.
[04:55] Jared: Pricing — we need an estimate for Dedicated seat and a pilot for 3 months. Can you share ballpark?
[04:59] Samira: Yes, we'll send a pilot pricing sheet. For Dedicated it's a combination of reserved GPU-hours plus per-token egress. We'll include burst pricing and expected SLOs.
[05:10] Priya: Can you share a deployment checklist for VPC peering and firewall rules?
[05:14] Aisha: We'll attach a VPC onboarding doc and a checklist — it's in the shared drive.
[05:19] Samira: I'll drop links: 1) SOC2 pack 2) VPC onboarding checklist 3) LangChain + LlamaIndex sample repo 4) pilot pricing spreadsheet.
[05:29] Carlos: We might need an NDA addendum for data residency testing, can legal coordinate after we see the security docs?
[05:36] Samira: Absolutely. We'll loop legal and your security.
[05:40] Evelyn: For the bench, we use a custom embedding flow; does Redwood support custom embedding models?
[05:45] Marcus: Yes — we support custom embedding models and model aliasing. Embedding pipelines can be pinned and cached. We'll check quantization recommendations for your model.
[05:57] Jared: Last: observability — we need per-route cost breakdown and token-level cost attribution. Is that possible?
[06:04] Marcus: Yes, Redwood Console provides token-level cost, per-route dashboards, and traces linked to requests. For Private we'll ship finer-grained telemetry.
[06:15] Samira: Great. Let's recap next steps.
[06:19] Marcus: We'll run a pilot bench w/ your LangChain prompts. Need prompt set and an ingress pattern sample.
[06:25] Priya: We'll share the prompt set and gateway config by end of week.
[06:30] Samira: I'll send SOC2, VPC checklist, Terraform modules, and a pilot pricing sheet.
[06:36] Jared: Sounds good. Can we aim for a pilot start next Monday?
[06:39] Samira: We can target that; Marcus will reach out with bench plan and timings.
[06:43] Aisha: I'll create a calendar invite for pilot kickoff.
[06:46] Carlos: Thanks all.
[06:48] Samira: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up in email with links and action items.

Notes: transcript includes some overlapping speech; some product names transcribed inconsistently ("Redwood Dedicate", "KV cash"). Links referenced during call: https://redwood.example.com/security/soc2, https://drive.example.com/lyrica/vpc-checklist, https://github.com/redwood-inference/langchain-examples, https://sheets.example.com/pilot-pricing-lyrica

Customer to review security docs and confirm legal requirements
